source_batch.unit_label: Module D unit 2 (courseware unit 27): compliance audit, disclosures, accounting standards and listing disclosures

facts.statement: Risk based internal audit (RBIA): the Institute of Internal Auditors defines it as a methodology that links internal auditing to the organisation's overall risk management framework and gives assurance to the board that risk management processes manage risks effectively in relation to the risk appetite. It is about auditing how risk is managed, not the risks themselves; its focus is the responses to individual risks and the processes used to assess risks, decide responses, monitor them and report to the board. All banks adopt RBIA in line with RBI requirements (the 2002 Guidance Note on RBIA). Its objectives include examining the internal control environment, reviewing inherent risks and the controls of the first and second lines, ensuring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, identifying control deficiencies and monitoring closure of action items, giving assurance to the Board, checking adherence to instructions, spotting dereliction of duty and transgression of powers, examining branch access from the angle of fraud vulnerability and assessing corporate governance. Breaches found in inspection are reported to the Chief Compliance Officer at central office with a copy to the risk management department and the regional or zonal head.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 571-572; RBI_HIA_2021 paragraph 1 for the RBIA requirement

facts.statement: Lines of defence: the first line is the risk takers (business functions), the second line is risk oversight (risk management and compliance), and the third line is risk assurance (internal audit); external audit and the supervisor are outside the three lines. The courseware's check question marks the statement that the supervisor is a fourth line of defence as incorrect. The Board approves strategy and ensures prudent risk management; governance and assurance functions act as strong internal defences.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 572, 591

facts.statement: Principles of an effective internal audit function (the courseware lists sixteen): independent assurance to the board and senior management on controls, risk and governance; independence of the function from audited activities, with standing and authority; professional competence; integrity; an internal audit policy; scope covering every activity including outsourced ones and every group entity; adequate coverage of regulatory matters; a permanent function (experts may be hired for assignments but responsibility stays with internal audit); Audit Committee oversight; Head of Internal Audit responsible for standards, ethics, confidentiality and competency; independent assessment of the controls of business and support units; the Board ultimately responsible for internal control and for the audit function even when experts are hired; each bank in a group has its own internal audit function accountable to its Board and reporting to the group head of internal audit, or the group function covers it sufficiently; a quality assurance and improvement programme covering all aspects.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 572-573

facts.statement: Fraud risk and internal audit: crores of rupees are lost to fraud each year, often because controls are poor and governance weak. Fraud risk is part of the audit plan and each assignment; the Head of Internal Audit considers how fraud risk is managed across the bank and assesses exposure periodically. Internal auditors need enough knowledge of fraud to identify red flags, understand fraud techniques, evaluate indicators and judge whether to recommend investigation, and to assess controls that prevent or detect fraud. They should not investigate fraud unless they have the specific experience and expertise, and conflicts of interest are avoided. The audit approach is risk based, assignment plans set objectives, scope, timing and resources, the Head of Internal Audit supervises, and compliance and its sustenance are monitored. All pending high and medium risk paragraphs are reported to the Board or Audit Committee of the Board; if management has accepted a level of risk that may be unacceptable to the bank, the Head of Internal Audit discusses it with senior management and escalates unresolved issues to the Board or Committee.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 573-574

facts.statement: Board and Audit Committee of the Board (courseware): the Board makes sure the audit function is properly positioned, staffed and equipped, respects the independence of audit reports (they reach the Board or the Committee without management filtering), and delegates implementation of the audit framework and review of policies to the Audit Committee. The Audit Committee is chaired by an independent person who is not the chair of the Board; includes members with audit, financial reporting and accounting experience; oversees financial reporting, recommends the appointment, remuneration and dismissal of external auditors, approves audit scope and frequency, follows up on corrective action, reviews the annual financial statements with the management letter, reviews audit reports and fraud and cash-shortage reports, meets the Head of internal audit and management, can retain expert advisers at the bank's expense, meets at least once a quarter, and a resolution needs two thirds of members in favour, with a dissenting member of a carried resolution giving a written statement to the Board.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 575-576

facts.statement: Head of Internal Audit (RBI circular of 7 January 2021, applicable to scheduled commercial banks other than RRBs, local area banks, small finance banks and payments banks): authority, stature and independence: the HIA is a senior executive able to exercise independent judgement, and the HIA and the function can communicate with any staff member and access all records and files needed. Competence: knowledge of banking operations, accounting, information technology, data analytics and forensic investigation, with the skills to audit all areas. Staff rotation: unless internal audit is a specialised function of career internal auditors, the Board prescribes a minimum period of service in internal audit and may require at least one stint for specialists posted elsewhere. Tenor: unless internal audit is a specialised function of career auditors, the HIA is appointed for a reasonably long period, preferably a minimum of three years.
facts.locator: RBI_HIA_2021 paragraph 3 (authority, competence, staff rotation, tenor)

facts.statement: HIA reporting line, remuneration and outsourcing (RBI circular of 7 January 2021): the HIA reports directly to the Audit Committee of the Board (ACB), the MD and CEO or a whole time director. If the Board lets the MD and CEO or a whole time director be the reporting authority, the reviewing authority is the ACB and the accepting authority is the Board for the HIA's performance appraisal, and the ACB meets the HIA at least once a quarter without senior management (including the MD and CEO or WTD). The HIA has no reporting relationship with business verticals and is given no business targets. In a foreign bank branch the HIA reports to the internal audit function of the controlling or head office. Remuneration of audit staff must not be linked to the financial performance of the business lines they audit. The internal audit function shall not be outsourced; experts, including former employees, may be hired on contract if the ACB is assured the expertise does not exist in the function, conflicts of interest are addressed, and ownership of audit reports always rests with regular functionaries of internal audit. The instructions took effect on the date of the circular.
facts.locator: RBI_HIA_2021 paragraphs 3 to 6 (reporting line, remuneration, outsourcing, effect)

facts.statement: Specialised audit verticals (courseware): offsite audit monitors certain transactions of branches or offices from the centre using MIS databases and query tools such as SQL and supports on-field auditors; information system audit covers all information systems (planning, organisation, acquisition, implementation, delivery and support), their process effectiveness, input and output controls and achievement of system goals; the concurrent audit function is responsible for satisfactory implementation of the concurrent audit system, including review and reporting of observations and their timely compliance. The courseware lists recent RBI initiatives: concurrent audit amendments, standing and independence of internal audit, mandatory RBIA for certain UCBs and NBFCs, compliance function strengthening, system based identification of NPAs and harmonised appointment of statutory auditors.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 577-578

facts.statement: Reporting framework for compliance (courseware, from RBI instructions): the reporting system covers the status or extent of compliance and the breaches or non-compliances found. Breaches are reported in a structured format by branches to the regional or zonal office, which sends them to the Compliance department at central office with a copy to the Field General Manager's Office; a copy of the certificate goes to the Risk officer for test checking on a random basis. Breaches can also be reported from officials' visits, audit reports and surveys. Functional departments at central office report their own breaches to the Compliance department; overseas branches follow the same system; the audit department gives the Compliance department a copy of its report on breaches, also furnished to the controlling regional or zonal office. For test checking the Risk officer uses the compliance certification and picks samples considering regulatory focus, whether the activity has inherent high risk, the bank's exposure, major breaches reported in the past, and does not repeat the same branches each time.
facts.locator: S01 printed p. 579

facts.statement: Applicability and purpose (2025 Directions): the disclosure framework lets market participants assess capital adequacy, risk exposures, risk assessment processes and key business parameters; it supplements and does not replace disclosure under other laws. The 2025 Directions apply to Commercial Banks, meaning banking companies other than Regional Rural Banks, Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks and Local Area Banks, corresponding new banks and the State Bank of India. They repealed the earlier Directions on financial statements for commercial banks, including the 2021 Master Direction the courseware describes.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 paragraph 3 and Chapter VI paragraph 31; S01 printed p. 580 for the purpose

facts.statement: Consolidated financial statements (CFS), 2025 Directions Chapter IV: in addition to standalone statements under section 29 of the Banking Regulation Act, a bank, listed or unlisted, prepares and discloses CFS in its annual report in the prescribed format; CFS normally include a consolidated balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, principal accounting policies and Notes to Accounts; CFS are submitted to the Department of Supervision, RBI, within one month of publishing the annual accounts; prepared under the applicable accounting standards; a parent consolidates all subsidiaries, domestic and foreign, except those the standards allow it to exclude; management decides inclusion and the reasons for not consolidating a subsidiary are disclosed; an RRB is treated as an associate in the CFS of its sponsor bank.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter IV paragraphs 11 to 15; S01 printed pp. 580-581

facts.statement: Inter-branch accounts (2025 Directions Chapter V.A): credit entries outstanding for more than five years are moved to a separate Blocked Account under Other Liabilities and Provisions - Others; any adjustment out of it needs authorisation by two officials, one from the Controlling or Head Office if the amount exceeds one lakh rupees; its balance is a liability for CRR and SLR; the bank keeps category-wise (head-wise) accounts for types of transactions so netting is category-wise; at the balance sheet date entries unreconciled for more than six months are segregated and the category-wise net position is found, considering the Blocked Account balance; net debits of all categories are aggregated and a provision of 100 per cent of the aggregate net debit is made, with no set-off of net debit in one category against net credit in another.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter V paragraph 19; S01 printed p. 581 items 7 and 8

facts.statement: Nostro accounts (2025 Directions Chapter V.B): the bank puts in strong reconciliation control with a real-time system and immediate escalation of differences; top management monitors pending items at short intervals; unreconciled credit entries outstanding for more than three years are transferred to a Blocked Account and shown as outstanding liabilities; the Blocked Account balance is reckoned for CRR and SLR; 100 per cent provision is made for unreconciled debit entries outstanding for more than two years.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter V paragraph 20; S01 printed p. 581 item 9

facts.statement: Reserves and appropriations (2025 Directions Chapter V.C): under sections 17(1) and 11(2)(b)(ii) of the Banking Regulation Act a bank transfers not less than 20 per cent of the profit disclosed in the profit and loss account to the Reserve Fund, as a minimum statutory requirement; to augment capital, a Commercial Bank transfers not less than 25 per cent of net profit before appropriations to the Statutory Reserve. Prior RBI approval is needed for any appropriation from the Statutory Reserve or another reserve unless regulations allow it. All expenses, including provisions and write-offs, are shown above the line before net profit; draw down from reserves with prior RBI approval is shown below the line and disclosed in Notes to Accounts. The share premium account may be used without RBI approval for incremental, directly attributable issue expenses of shares, but not for expenses of issuing debt instruments.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter V paragraphs 21 to 23; S01 printed p. 581 items 10 to 12

facts.statement: Fraud provisioning, unclaimed balances and window dressing (2025 Directions Chapter V.D, E, G): a bank that reports a fraud within the prescribed time may provide for it over a period not exceeding four quarters starting from the quarter of detection; if this spreads over more than one financial year it may debit reserves other than the Statutory Reserve for the un-provided amount and later reverse the debits proportionately, completing the provision through the profit and loss account in the next year's quarters; where reporting of the fraud to RBI is delayed beyond the prescribed period, the entire provision is made at once. Unreconciled credit balances in a transitory account representing unclaimed balances are not transferred to the profit and loss account or any reserve. Window dressing of financials, short provisioning, NPA misclassification, under-reporting of exposure or risk weight, incorrect capitalisation of expenses or of interest on NPAs, and year-end inflation of assets and liabilities reversed in the next year are viewed seriously, with penal action under the Banking Regulation Act considered.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter V paragraphs 24 to 30; S01 printed pp. 581-582

facts.statement: Penalty disclosure (2025 Directions, Notes to Accounts item 12): penalties imposed by RBI under the Banking Regulation Act 1949, the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007 and the Government Securities Act 2006 (for bouncing of SGL) are disclosed in the Notes to Accounts of the concerned bank's next annual report, including the nature of the breach, the number of instances and the quantum of penalty; a foreign bank discloses in the Notes to Accounts for its Indian operations.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter III, Notes to Accounts item (12); S01 printed p. 582

facts.statement: Other Notes to Accounts disclosures (2025 Directions): provision coverage ratio and sector-wise advances and gross NPAs; concentration of the twenty largest depositors, borrowers, exposures and NPA accounts; Letters of Comfort issued (full particulars, assessed financial impact and cumulative obligations); intra-group exposures (total, top 20, percentage of total exposure to borrowers and customers, and breaches of limits with regulatory action); unhedged foreign currency exposure (policies, incremental provisioning and capital held); liquidity coverage ratio for all four quarters with qualitative information; securitisation, bancassurance fees and brokerage, customer complaints including Ombudsman awards, transfers to the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund, floating provisions and remuneration (private sector and foreign banks).
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter III Notes to Accounts; S01 printed pp. 584-585

facts.statement: Segment reporting (AS 17, 2025 Directions): the business segment is ordinarily the primary format and the geographical segment the secondary one. The business segments are Treasury, Corporate or Wholesale Banking, Retail Banking and Other Banking Business; the geographic segments are Domestic and International. Treasury includes the entire investment portfolio; Retail Banking includes exposures meeting the retail criteria (orientation, product, granularity, low value) and individual housing loans; Corporate or Wholesale Banking includes advances to trusts, partnership firms, companies and statutory bodies not in Retail; Other Banking Business includes everything else, including para banking activities.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter II.C, AS 17; S01 printed p. 582

facts.statement: Other accounting standards for banks (2025 Directions): AS 5 prior period items: all banks comply for any prior period income or expenditure item exceeding one per cent of total income or total expenditure (gross basis) or one per cent of net profit before taxes or net loss (net basis), and the impact is disclosed in Notes to Accounts because Form B has no line for it. AS 9: non-recognition of income on non-performing advances and investments under RBI norms does not attract an auditor's qualification. AS 23: holding 20 per cent or more of voting power raises a presumption of significant influence; a bank that converts debt to equity and holds over 20 per cent may show its rights are protective, not participative, and then need not treat the holding as an associate, because the test is the intention to exercise significant influence and not only the proportion held. AS 25: listed banks' quarterly results are not interim reporting under AS 25 and AS 25 is not mandatory for them, but its recognition and measurement principles must be followed. AS 18 requires related party disclosures in a prescribed illustrative format; AS 24: merger or closure of branches within the same bank is not a discontinuing operation.
facts.locator: RBI_FS_2025 Chapter II.C, AS 5, 9, 18, 23, 24, 25; S01 printed pp. 582-583

facts.statement: SEBI Listing Regulations (courseware): a company that wants its securities listed signs a Listing Agreement with the exchange; the disclosure requirements of the Listing Agreement were incorporated into the SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015, effective 90 days from 2 September 2015. They apply to a listed entity with designated securities: specified securities on the main board or SME exchange or Innovators Growth Platform, non-convertible securities, Indian depository receipts, securitised debt instruments and security receipts, units of mutual funds and any others the Board specifies. Principles: information prepared and disclosed per applicable accounting standards, with an independent audit; no misrepresentation; adequate and timely disclosure; accurate, explicit, timely and simple dissemination; equal, timely and cost-efficient access for investors; filings carrying relevant information; compliance with applicable laws and SEBI guidelines.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 585-586

facts.statement: Prior intimation under Regulation 29 (courseware): a listed entity gives the exchanges prior intimation of board meetings that will consider financial results (quarterly, half-yearly or annual), a buyback, voluntary delisting, fund raising by any method with the issue price decision, dividend or the issue of convertible securities (including debentures or debentures with a right to subscribe to equity), and any alteration in the form or nature of listed securities or in the date, interest or redemption amount on debentures or bonds. Intimation is also given where an AGM, EGM or postal ballot is proposed for approving fund raising. The courseware gives different notice periods for different proposals (two working days, five days for results, eleven working days for alterations); secondary reports say a 2024 amendment made it at least two clear working days for all, which could not be verified at SEBI.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 586-587

facts.statement: Disclosure of events under Regulation 30 (courseware): events fall into two categories. Para A events must be disclosed without applying any test of materiality, for example acquisition or sale of a unit or division and schemes of arrangement; issue, forfeiture, buyback, split or consolidation of securities and restrictions on their transfer; new or revised ratings; outcomes of board meetings; certain shareholder, joint venture or family settlement agreements that affect management and control; fraud or default by the promoter, key managerial personnel or the entity, or arrest of key managerial personnel or promoter; change in directors, key managerial personnel, auditor and compliance officer; resolution plan or restructuring of loans; one time settlement with a bank; winding-up petitions; notices to security holders; proceedings of general meetings; amendments to the memorandum and articles; schedule of analyst or institutional investor meetings. Para B events are disclosed if considered material, for example commencement or postponement of commercial production, strategic tie-ups, capacity addition or product launch, award or termination of orders, disruption of operations by natural calamity or strikes, effect of regulatory change, pending litigation, fraud or default by directors (other than key managerial personnel) or employees, guarantees or indemnity for third parties, grant, withdrawal or suspension of licences, and delay or default in paying fines or penalties to regulators.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 587-588

facts.statement: Other listing information (courseware): other regulations require, among others, holding of specified securities and shareholding pattern (Regulation 31), financial results (Regulation 33), the annual report (Regulation 34), the draft scheme of arrangement and sale, lease or disposal of an undertaking outside a scheme (Regulations 37 and 37A), minimum public shareholding (Regulation 38) and record date or closure of transfer books (Regulation 42). Regulation 46 requires a website with details of the business, the Memorandum and Articles, board profile, terms of appointment of independent directors, committee composition, codes of conduct, vigil mechanism or whistle-blower policy, related party transaction policy, material subsidiaries policy, familiarisation programmes for independent directors, grievance contacts, financial information, shareholding pattern and investor meet schedules, updated within two days of any change. Regulation 47 requires an advertisement in the newspaper after the board meeting that approves financial results, giving a quick response code and the web page where the results are available.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 589-590

payload.title: Risk based internal audit
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Risk based internal audit (RBIA)** ties audit work to the bank's **risk management framework**. It gives the **Board** assurance that the processes for **identifying, assessing, responding to, monitoring and reporting** risk work properly against the **risk appetite**.

- It audits **how risk is managed**, not the risks as such.
- Every bank adopts it, in line with RBI's requirements.

**What it sets out to do:** test the **control environment**, review the **controls of the first and second lines**, confirm **legal and regulatory compliance**, find **control gaps** and follow their **closure**, spot **dereliction of duty** and **excess use of powers**, check where branches are **exposed to fraud**, and assure the Board on **governance** and **risk management**.

When an audit finds **breaches**, the report goes to the **Chief Compliance Officer** at the central office, with a copy to **risk management** and to the **regional or zonal head**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware stresses that the audit looks at the management of risk, which is why the Board relies on it for assurance and not for risk taking.

self_check.prompt_text: What does risk based internal audit examine?
self_check.expected_takeaway: How the bank manages risk: the processes for assessing, responding to, monitoring and reporting it, not the risks themselves.

payload.title: The three lines of defence
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Line | Who | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **First** | **Business functions** (risk takers) | Own and manage the risk they take |
| **Second** | **Risk management and compliance** | **Oversee** the risk |
| **Third** | **Internal audit** | Give **independent assurance** |

**External audit** and the **supervisor** sit **outside** the three lines. A statement that the supervisor is a **fourth line** is the one the courseware treats as **wrong**.

The **Board and senior management** set strategy and make sure risk is run prudently; the governance and assurance functions are the bank's **internal defences**, which RBI has strengthened through recent instructions.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Compliance is a second-line function, so a business head cannot also act as the compliance officer without breaking the separation.

self_check.prompt_text: Which line of defence does internal audit form?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The third line, risk assurance.

payload.title: Principles of an effective internal audit function
payload.core_explanation_md:
Held at needs_review: the courseware lists **sixteen principles**. In groups:

| Theme | Principle |
| --- | --- |
| **Assurance** | Independent assurance to the **Board and senior management** |
| **Independence and standing** | Independent of audited activities, with **authority** |
| **People** | **Competence** and **integrity** |
| **Policy and scope** | A **policy**; scope covers **every activity (including outsourced) and every group entity**; adequate cover of **regulatory matters** |
| **Permanence** | A **permanent** function; **experts** may help but **responsibility stays** with internal audit |
| **Oversight** | **Audit Committee** oversees; the **Head of Internal Audit** upholds standards and ethics |
| **Board** | **Ultimately responsible** for internal control, even when experts are hired |
| **Group** | Each bank has **its own function**, or the group function covers it |
| **Quality** | A **quality assurance and improvement programme** |
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The principles follow the international guidance the courseware refers to; the exact count and wording are the courseware's.

self_check.prompt_text: Who remains ultimately responsible when experts are hired for internal audit?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Board of Directors.

payload.title: Internal audit and fraud risk
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Auditors assess whether controls would prevent or detect fraud; they are not the bank's fraud investigators by default.

self_check.prompt_text: To whom are unresolved, unacceptable risks accepted by management escalated?
self_check.expected_takeaway: To the Board or its Audit Committee, after the Head of Internal Audit has discussed them with senior management.

payload.title: The Board and the Audit Committee of the Board
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The two-thirds rule and written dissent are the courseware's account and are held pending the source.

self_check.prompt_text: What majority does a resolution of the Audit Committee need under the courseware?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The affirmative votes of two thirds of the members.

payload.title: Rules for the Head of Internal Audit
payload.core_explanation_md:
RBI circular of **7 January 2021** (scheduled commercial banks other than RRBs, plus LABs, SFBs and payments banks):

| Topic | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | **Senior executive**, able to use **independent judgement**; access to **any staff** and **all records** |
| **Competence** | Banking, accounting, **IT**, **data analytics**, **forensics** |
| **Staff rotation** | **Minimum period of service** set by the Board (unless career auditors) |
| **Tenor** | **Reasonably long**, **preferably at least 3 years** (unless career auditors) |
| **Reports to** | **ACB**, **MD and CEO** or **whole time director** |
| **If MD and CEO or WTD reports** | **Reviewing authority: ACB**; **accepting authority: Board**; **ACB meets HIA quarterly without senior management** |
| **Business link** | **None**: no business vertical, **no business targets** |
| **Foreign bank branch** | Reports to the **controlling or head office** internal audit |
| **Pay** | Not linked to the **business lines audited** |
| **Outsourcing** | **Internal audit is not outsourced**; experts on contract only if the **ACB** is assured the skill is absent, with **report ownership** staying with regular staff |
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The circular took effect on its own date and supplements the 2002 Guidance Note on risk based internal audit.

self_check.prompt_text: May a bank outsource its internal audit function?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No; it may only hire experts on contract if the ACB is assured the expertise is not available in the function.

payload.title: Offsite, IS and concurrent audit
payload.core_explanation_md:
The courseware describes three verticals inside internal audit:

- **Offsite audit:** monitors **branch and office transactions from the centre**, using **MIS databases** and tools such as **SQL**, and feeds the **on-field auditors**.
- **Information system (IS) audit:** covers **all information systems**, their **process effectiveness**, **input and output controls** and **goal achievement**.
- **Concurrent audit:** the function that makes sure the **concurrent audit system** works, reviews observations and ensures **timely compliance**.

RBI's recent supervisory reforms, as the courseware lists them, cover **concurrent audit**, **standing of internal audit**, **RBIA** for certain UCBs and NBFCs, **strengthening compliance**, **system based NPA identification** and **appointment of statutory auditors**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Offsite audit reduces the load on field auditors by flagging unusual transactions from the centre.

self_check.prompt_text: What tool does the offsite audit team use to query the MIS databases?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Tools such as SQL.

payload.title: Reporting and test checking of compliance breaches
payload.core_explanation_md:
Held at needs_review (courseware).

**Reporting path:** **branch** → **regional or zonal office** → **Compliance department at central office** (copy to the **Field General Manager's Office**). Breaches come from **branch reports**, **officials' visits**, **audit reports** and **surveys**. **Functional departments at central office** report their own breaches; **overseas branches** follow the same path; **audit** sends the Compliance department a copy of its breach report.

**Test checking:** the **Risk officer** takes a **random sample** of branches from the **compliance certificates** and tests them independently. Sampling weighs **regulatory focus**, **inherent high-risk activity**, the **bank's exposure** and **past major breaches**, and **does not repeat the same branches** each time.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Certificates alone could be wrong, so independent test checking confirms they reflect reality.

self_check.prompt_text: Which officer test checks the compliance certificates at random?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Risk officer.

payload.title: Disclosure framework and consolidated statements
payload.expanded_explanation_md: RRBs, small finance banks, payments banks and LABs follow their own Directions, not the commercial bank ones.

self_check.prompt_text: How is an RRB treated in its sponsor bank's consolidated statements?
self_check.expected_takeaway: As an associate.

payload.title: Blocked accounts: inter-branch and Nostro entries
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Item | Inter-branch accounts | Nostro accounts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Credits moved to a Blocked Account** | Outstanding **over 5 years** | Outstanding **over 3 years** |
| **Debit entries** | Unreconciled over **6 months**, netted **category-wise** | Unreconciled over **2 years** |
| **Provision** | **100%** of the **aggregate net debit** | **100%** of those debits |
| **Blocked Account for CRR/SLR** | **Counts as a liability** | **Counts** |
| **Release of Blocked Account** | **Two officials**, one from **Controlling or Head Office** if above **Rs 1 lakh** | n/a |

**No set-off across categories:** a net debit in one category cannot be reduced by a net credit in another. For Nostro accounts, put in **real-time reconciliation** and have **top management** watch pending items.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The Blocked Account is shown under Other Liabilities and Provisions - Others for inter-branch credits.

self_check.prompt_text: After how many years are unreconciled Nostro credits moved to a Blocked Account?
self_check.expected_takeaway: More than three years.

payload.title: Provisioning and appropriations: a year-end walk-through
payload.core_explanation_md:
A commercial bank closes its year with these inter-branch entries unreconciled for more than six months (Rs crore):

| Category | Debits | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | 6.0 | 4.5 |
| **B** | 2.0 | 3.0 |
| **C** | 1.2 | 0.7 |

Its Nostro accounts hold a debit entry of **Rs 40 lakh** outstanding for **2 years 3 months** and a credit entry of **Rs 25 lakh** outstanding for **3 years 2 months**. Its profit disclosed in the profit and loss account is **Rs 480 crore**. Find the inter-branch provision, the Nostro treatment and the transfers.

worked_steps.description: Net each category on its own: A is a net debit, B a net credit, C a net debit.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: Net debits in A and C only

worked_steps.description: Add the net debits without setting off B's net credit.
Provide 100 per cent of the aggregate net debit.
Nostro debit entry has been outstanding for more than two years.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: 100 per cent provision of Rs 40 lakh

worked_steps.description: Nostro credit entry has been outstanding for more than three years.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: Rs 25 lakh moves to a Blocked Account (counts for CRR and SLR)

worked_steps.description: Statutory minimum transfer to the Reserve Fund is 20 per cent of profit; a commercial bank transfers at least 25 per cent to the Statutory Reserve.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: At least Rs 120 crore to the Statutory Reserve

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Inter-branch provision Rs 2.0 crore (not Rs 1.0 crore); Nostro debit fully provided (Rs 40 lakh); Nostro credit of Rs 25 lakh to the Blocked Account; at least Rs 120 crore to the Statutory Reserve

self_check.prompt_text: What would the provision wrongly be if category B's net credit were set off?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Rs 1.0 crore (2.0 - 1.0), which the Directions do not allow.

payload.title: Reserves, fraud provisioning and window dressing
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Reserves (2025 Directions):**

- **At least 20%** of profit to the **Reserve Fund** (Banking Regulation Act minimum).
- A **commercial bank** moves **at least 25% of net profit before appropriations** to the **Statutory Reserve**.
- **Prior RBI approval** for any use of the Statutory Reserve or another reserve, unless allowed by regulation.
- **Expenses and provisions** are **above the line**; **approved draw down from reserves** is **below the line** and disclosed.
- **Share premium** may meet **incremental, directly attributable share issue costs** without approval, **never debt issue costs**.

**Fraud provisioning:** reported **on time** → provide over **up to four quarters** from the quarter of detection (spanning years: debit **non-statutory reserves** and reverse later); **late report** → **full provision at once**.

**Other rules:** **unclaimed credits in transitory accounts** never go to profit or reserves. **Window dressing**, short provisioning, NPA misclassification and the like draw **penal action** under the Banking Regulation Act.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Delay in reporting a fraud removes the instalment benefit, which pushes banks to report fast.

payload.title: Material events (Regulation 30)
payload.core_explanation_md:
Held at needs_review (courseware lists; the Schedule has been amended since).

**Para A: disclose always, no materiality test.** Examples: **acquisitions and sales of units, schemes of arrangement**; **issue, forfeiture, buyback, split of securities**; **new or revised ratings**; **board meeting outcomes**; **fraud or default** by the **promoter, KMP or entity**, or **arrest of KMP or promoter**; **change in directors, KMP, auditor or compliance officer**; **loan restructuring or resolution plan**; **one time settlement** with a bank; **winding-up petition**; **proceedings of general meetings**; **amendments to the memorandum and articles**.

**Para B: disclose only if material.** Examples: **start or postponement of production**; **strategic tie-ups**; **capacity addition or product launch**; **order wins and cancellations**; **disruption from calamity or strikes**; **regulatory change**; **pending litigation**; **fraud by directors (not KMP) or employees**; **guarantees for third parties**; **licence grant, withdrawal or suspension**; **delay or default in paying penalties**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The distinction is whether the entity may judge materiality: for Para A events it may not.

self_check.expected_takeaway: No; it is a Para A event, disclosed without a materiality test.

items.title: Risk based internal audit
items.core_explanation_md:
**Risk based internal audit (RBIA)** ties audit work to the bank's **risk management framework**. It gives the **Board** assurance that the processes for **identifying, assessing, responding to, monitoring and reporting** risk work properly against the **risk appetite**.

- It audits **how risk is managed**, not the risks as such.
- Every bank adopts it, in line with RBI's requirements.

**What it sets out to do:** test the **control environment**, review the **controls of the first and second lines**, confirm **legal and regulatory compliance**, find **control gaps** and follow their **closure**, spot **dereliction of duty** and **excess use of powers**, check where branches are **exposed to fraud**, and assure the Board on **governance** and **risk management**.

When an audit finds **breaches**, the report goes to the **Chief Compliance Officer** at the central office, with a copy to **risk management** and to the **regional or zonal head**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware stresses that the audit looks at the management of risk, which is why the Board relies on it for assurance and not for risk taking.

self_check.prompt_text: What does risk based internal audit examine?
self_check.expected_takeaway: How the bank manages risk: the processes for assessing, responding to, monitoring and reporting it, not the risks themselves.

items.title: The three lines of defence
items.core_explanation_md:
| Line | Who | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **First** | **Business functions** (risk takers) | Own and manage the risk they take |
| **Second** | **Risk management and compliance** | **Oversee** the risk |
| **Third** | **Internal audit** | Give **independent assurance** |

**External audit** and the **supervisor** sit **outside** the three lines. A statement that the supervisor is a **fourth line** is the one the courseware treats as **wrong**.

The **Board and senior management** set strategy and make sure risk is run prudently; the governance and assurance functions are the bank's **internal defences**, which RBI has strengthened through recent instructions.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Compliance is a second-line function, so a business head cannot also act as the compliance officer without breaking the separation.

self_check.expected_takeaway: The third line, risk assurance.

RBI circular of **7 January 2021** (scheduled commercial banks other than RRBs, plus LABs, SFBs and payments banks):

| Topic | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | **Senior executive**, able to use **independent judgement**; access to **any staff** and **all records** |
| **Competence** | Banking, accounting, **IT**, **data analytics**, **forensics** |
| **Staff rotation** | **Minimum period of service** set by the Board (unless career auditors) |
| **Tenor** | **Reasonably long**, **preferably at least 3 years** (unless career auditors) |
| **Reports to** | **ACB**, **MD and CEO** or **whole time director** |
| **If MD and CEO or WTD reports** | **Reviewing authority: ACB**; **accepting authority: Board**; **ACB meets HIA quarterly without senior management** |
| **Business link** | **None**: no business vertical, **no business targets** |
| **Foreign bank branch** | Reports to the **controlling or head office** internal audit |
| **Pay** | Not linked to the **business lines audited** |
| **Outsourcing** | **Internal audit is not outsourced**; experts on contract only if the **ACB** is assured the skill is absent, with **report ownership** staying with regular staff |
items.expanded_explanation_md: The circular took effect on its own date and supplements the 2002 Guidance Note on risk based internal audit.

self_check.prompt_text: May a bank outsource its internal audit function?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No; it may only hire experts on contract if the ACB is assured the expertise is not available in the function.

items.title: Offsite, IS and concurrent audit
items.core_explanation_md:
The courseware describes three verticals inside internal audit:

- **Offsite audit:** monitors **branch and office transactions from the centre**, using **MIS databases** and tools such as **SQL**, and feeds the **on-field auditors**.
- **Information system (IS) audit:** covers **all information systems**, their **process effectiveness**, **input and output controls** and **goal achievement**.
- **Concurrent audit:** the function that makes sure the **concurrent audit system** works, reviews observations and ensures **timely compliance**.

RBI's recent supervisory reforms, as the courseware lists them, cover **concurrent audit**, **standing of internal audit**, **RBIA** for certain UCBs and NBFCs, **strengthening compliance**, **system based NPA identification** and **appointment of statutory auditors**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Offsite audit reduces the load on field auditors by flagging unusual transactions from the centre.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Tools such as SQL.

items.title: Reporting and test checking of compliance breaches
items.core_explanation_md:
Held at needs_review (courseware).

**Reporting path:** **branch** → **regional or zonal office** → **Compliance department at central office** (copy to the **Field General Manager's Office**). Breaches come from **branch reports**, **officials' visits**, **audit reports** and **surveys**. **Functional departments at central office** report their own breaches; **overseas branches** follow the same path; **audit** sends the Compliance department a copy of its breach report.

**Test checking:** the **Risk officer** takes a **random sample** of branches from the **compliance certificates** and tests them independently. Sampling weighs **regulatory focus**, **inherent high-risk activity**, the **bank's exposure** and **past major breaches**, and **does not repeat the same branches** each time.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Certificates alone could be wrong, so independent test checking confirms they reflect reality.

self_check.prompt_text: Which officer test checks the compliance certificates at random?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Risk officer.

items.title: Provisioning and appropriations: a year-end walk-through
items.core_explanation_md:
A commercial bank closes its year with these inter-branch entries unreconciled for more than six months (Rs crore):

| Category | Debits | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | 6.0 | 4.5 |
| **B** | 2.0 | 3.0 |
| **C** | 1.2 | 0.7 |

Its Nostro accounts hold a debit entry of **Rs 40 lakh** outstanding for **2 years 3 months** and a credit entry of **Rs 25 lakh** outstanding for **3 years 2 months**. Its profit disclosed in the profit and loss account is **Rs 480 crore**. Find the inter-branch provision, the Nostro treatment and the transfers.

worked_steps.description: Net each category on its own: A is a net debit, B a net credit, C a net debit.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: Net debits in A and C only

worked_steps.description: Add the net debits without setting off B's net credit.
Provide 100 per cent of the aggregate net debit.
Nostro debit entry has been outstanding for more than two years.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: 100 per cent provision of Rs 40 lakh

worked_steps.description: Nostro credit entry has been outstanding for more than three years.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: Rs 25 lakh moves to a Blocked Account (counts for CRR and SLR)

worked_steps.description: Statutory minimum transfer to the Reserve Fund is 20 per cent of profit; a commercial bank transfers at least 25 per cent to the Statutory Reserve.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: At least Rs 120 crore to the Statutory Reserve

items.final_answer_with_unit: Inter-branch provision Rs 2.0 crore (not Rs 1.0 crore); Nostro debit fully provided (Rs 40 lakh); Nostro credit of Rs 25 lakh to the Blocked Account; at least Rs 120 crore to the Statutory Reserve

items.title: Reserves, fraud provisioning and window dressing
items.core_explanation_md:
**Reserves (2025 Directions):**

- **At least 20%** of profit to the **Reserve Fund** (Banking Regulation Act minimum).
- A **commercial bank** moves **at least 25% of net profit before appropriations** to the **Statutory Reserve**.
- **Prior RBI approval** for any use of the Statutory Reserve or another reserve, unless allowed by regulation.
- **Expenses and provisions** are **above the line**; **approved draw down from reserves** is **below the line** and disclosed.
- **Share premium** may meet **incremental, directly attributable share issue costs** without approval, **never debt issue costs**.

**Fraud provisioning:** reported **on time** → provide over **up to four quarters** from the quarter of detection (spanning years: debit **non-statutory reserves** and reverse later); **late report** → **full provision at once**.

**Other rules:** **unclaimed credits in transitory accounts** never go to profit or reserves. **Window dressing**, short provisioning, NPA misclassification and the like draw **penal action** under the Banking Regulation Act.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Delay in reporting a fraud removes the instalment benefit, which pushes banks to report fast.

self_check.prompt_text: Over how many quarters at most can a timely reported fraud be provided for?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Four quarters, starting from the quarter in which it was detected.

items.title: Listing Regulations: scope and principles
items.core_explanation_md:
Held at needs_review (courseware).

A company that lists its shares signs a **Listing Agreement** with the exchange. Its disclosure duties now sit in the **SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015**, effective **90 days after 2 September 2015**.

**Covered securities:** **equity on the main board or SME exchange**, **non-convertible securities**, **IDRs**, **securitised debt and security receipts**, **mutual fund units**.

**Principles:** information per **accounting standards** with an **independent audit**; **no misrepresentation**; **adequate, timely, accurate, explicit and simple** disclosure; **equal, timely, low cost access** for investors; filings carry **relevant** information; obey **all applicable laws**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Banks listed on an exchange follow these Regulations in addition to RBI rules.

self_check.expected_takeaway: The SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015.

items.title: Material events (Regulation 30)
items.core_explanation_md:
Held at needs_review (courseware lists; the Schedule has been amended since).

**Para A: disclose always, no materiality test.** Examples: **acquisitions and sales of units, schemes of arrangement**; **issue, forfeiture, buyback, split of securities**; **new or revised ratings**; **board meeting outcomes**; **fraud or default** by the **promoter, KMP or entity**, or **arrest of KMP or promoter**; **change in directors, KMP, auditor or compliance officer**; **loan restructuring or resolution plan**; **one time settlement** with a bank; **winding-up petition**; **proceedings of general meetings**; **amendments to the memorandum and articles**.

**Para B: disclose only if material.** Examples: **start or postponement of production**; **strategic tie-ups**; **capacity addition or product launch**; **order wins and cancellations**; **disruption from calamity or strikes**; **regulatory change**; **pending litigation**; **fraud by directors (not KMP) or employees**; **guarantees for third parties**; **licence grant, withdrawal or suspension**; **delay or default in paying penalties**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The distinction is whether the entity may judge materiality: for Para A events it may not.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a change in the statutory auditor need a materiality test before disclosure?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No; it is a Para A event, disclosed without a materiality test.
